$comment: The crate half of the architecture map, read by `cargo xtask arch-map`. Every crate of the target graph is listed, planned ones included, so dependency direction is fixed before any code exists. A layer may depend only on the layers in its mayDependOn; a crate only on its allowedInternalDeps. A crate path must sit under one of its layer's dirs. Adapters never reach mechanics: ADR-0018 holds by construction.

core.description: pure, no I/O, unchanged on wasm32 and native

ports.description: the only route to I/O: async traits and the error taxonomy

adapters.description: translate HTTP and MCP to ops, and nothing else

mechanics.description: port implementations over a concrete store

bindings.description: composition roots: wasm-bindgen, workers-rs, the native daemon

tooling.description: repository tooling, test utilities and fuzz targets, never shipped

whiteboard-det.description: JS-compatible number formatting, pinned math, UTF-16 helpers, seeded randomness, ordered collections

allowedThirdParty.libm: fdlibm sin and cos, pure Rust and no_std, so they run unchanged on wasm32 and native; pinned exactly because canvas-render's det-math.ts is held to its bits

whiteboard-log.description: RFC 5424 levels, records, sinks and the fields-first logging macro

whiteboard-model.description: serde types generated from contracts/model plus the invariants a schema cannot express, and JSON text read as JSON.parse reads it (key order kept)

whiteboard-facet-engine.description: facet registry, write validation, compat chain, derived forms, theme tokens

whiteboard-scene.description: the scene vocabulary and the contribution traits

allowedThirdParty.serde: the Deserialize derive behind the `oracle` feature, so a test can replay the scenes the TypeScript recorded; no shipped build enables it, and it is no I/O and builds unchanged on wasm32 and native

whiteboard-codec.description: OKF Markdown, JSON Canvas and OCIF serialize and parse

whiteboard-markdown.description: CommonMark, GFM and math markdown parsed to an mdast tree: a vendored, trimmed and hardened copy of markdown-rs (MIT), with the cost, depth and totality bounds a wasm instance needs

whiteboard-search.description: tokenizer, BM25 ranking, snippets, searchable text; the Unicode it asks of is generated data (src/tables.rs), the pinned crates being dev-dependencies that generate and check it

allowedThirdParty.unicode-segmentation: UAX #29 grapheme clusters, where an excerpt may be cut, pinned exactly (QR-20b); the plugin-visual entry's review; Unicode 17.0, the release Node 24's ICU carries, and it agrees with Intl.Segmenter on every recorded case

whiteboard-plugin-visual.description: the bundled visual plugin as an ordinary contribution implementer

allowedThirdParty.unicode-segmentation: UAX #29 grapheme clusters for the single_grapheme check, pinned exactly (QR-20b); checked before adopting: MIT OR Apache-2.0, no dependencies, std or no_std, no I/O, `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`, tables only, so it builds unchanged on wasm32 and native; its tables are Unicode 17.0, the release Node 24's ICU carries

whiteboard-edge-routing.description: side choice, anchors, grid search, crossings, jumps, rounding, label anchor, budget, route cache

allowedThirdParty.serde: the derive the generated contract types use (contracts/geometry); no I/O, builds unchanged on wasm32 and native

whiteboard-canvas-render.description: composer, typesetter, line breaking, theme, SVG backend, sceneDigest, references

allowedThirdParty.unicode-segmentation: UAX #29 grapheme clusters for the cut between graphemes in fit_to_width, pinned exactly (QR-20b); checked before adopting: MIT OR Apache-2.0, no dependencies, std or no_std, no I/O, `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`, tables only, so it builds unchanged on wasm32 and native; its tables are Unicode 17.0, the release Node 24's ICU carries (the plugin-visual entry's review)

whiteboard-crdt.description: the loro bridge, workspace tree, file references, text-limit judge; today the reading of the bytes npm loro-crdt writes (deep value, version vector, frontiers) the tree and map writers the document index writes a workspace record with, and the document engine's content queries (kind, body and marks, locks, facets, the canvas with the records its schema refuses, core and trust facets, the annotation threads and their marks, proposals, image references, retired shapes) over a document that is the root of its own LoroDoc, native-only until the wasm export lands

allowedThirdParty.loro: the CRDT itself: the Rust crate npm loro-crdt is built from, pinned exactly in lock-step with the npm version (ADR-0054 decision 13; tools/arch-lint's loro-lock-step test compares the lockfiles, loro-internal included, which the manifest pin alone leaves floating); pure Rust with no I/O, but its tree reaches randomness (getrandom, rand: a peer id per document) and wasm-bindgen on wasm32, so deny.toml records scoped exceptions for loro's tree alone (MPL-2.0 im, sized-chunks and bitmaps, BSL-1.0 xxhash-rust, four unmaintained advisories, getrandom and rand through loro's crates only) and xtask's CORE_IMPORT_ALLOWANCES lets this crate alone import wasm-bindgen's modules; the artifact that links it must supply randomness from its host

whiteboard-history.description: version retention, the compaction cut and frontier encoding, over a record's bytes through whiteboard-crdt (checkpoint scheduling is a host timer and is not ported)

whiteboard-workspace-index.description: the document index's pure rules over a workspace tree (names, paths, moves, entries) and its reads over a workspace record's bytes (listings, resolves, trash, the restore judgement) and its writes over it (create, move, name, pin, folder names, delete, purge, restore, duplicate), each appending the operations the TypeScript index appends

allowedThirdParty.unicode-normalization: NFC for the display-name key, pure and no_std-capable so it holds on native and wasm32 alike; pinned exactly with default features off, as the search crate's generator pins it

whiteboard-reference-graph.description: per-document reference facts and the backlink aggregate (the pure rules; the cache over a port waits for the ports layer)

whiteboard-ports.description: the contracts an operation reaches I/O through: the error taxonomy, the MaybeSend bound, and the Clock, IdMint and WorkspaceLock traits; the store, index, blob, scheduler and measurement ports join as their first operation needs them

whiteboard-api-contracts.description: the refusal enum generated from contracts/api/refusals.json (code, status and the TypeScript's exact sentence per refusal) and the mapping from a port's failure to it; the types for /api, sync frames and MCP tool I/O follow

whiteboard-ops.description: every /api/v1 operation and MCP tool as a transport-neutral execute over ports; the tool table as data

whiteboard-http.description: an axum router over ops, mounted natively and on Workers

whiteboard-mcp.description: a transport-agnostic JSON-RPC dispatcher over the ops tool table

whiteboard-daemon-store.description: SQLite record store, fs blob store, versions, migrations, file GC, security stores, export

whiteboard-edge-store.description: Durable Object, D1 and R2 stores

whiteboard-wasm.description: the wasm-bindgen cdylib for the browser and Node; render and full artifacts by feature

allowedThirdParty.wasm-bindgen: the JS boundary itself; pinned = to the wasm-bindgen-cli that post-processes the artifact
allowedThirdParty.serde_json: the OKF exports' document wire: a frontmatter value is arbitrary nested data, which no flat typed array holds. Pure Rust, no I/O, runs unchanged on wasm32 and native; deny.toml already bans unbounded_depth and arbitrary_precision, so the 128-level recursion limit is part of the entry's depth cap

whiteboard-worker.description: the workers-rs app: router, MCP over HTTP, edge store, alarms

whiteboard-daemon.description: the native daemon binary: UDS server, MCP stdio, native-messaging host, PNG export

xtask.description: repository tasks: codegen, architecture map, wasm import scan, the core crates' cross-target tests, size and unsafe ledgers, fuzz registry, release gates (harden-check, repro-check, dist)

allowedThirdParty.serde: deserializes the architecture map and the size ledger
allowedThirdParty.serde_json: reads cargo metadata and the checked-in JSON ledgers
allowedThirdParty.wasmparser: reads a wasm artifact's import section for the core import scan
allowedThirdParty.object: reads a native binary's ELF headers, segments and dynamic table for harden-check (read-only, std + elf features only)

whiteboard-proptest.description: the one proptest prelude (QR-14b/d/e): the case budget, an unseeded runner, regressions beside the property, the reachability floor; a dev-dependency only

allowedThirdParty.proptest: the property runner (QR-14); std only, no fork or timeout, so the same property runs natively and on wasm32 under Node
allowedThirdParty.getrandom: wasm32 only, with wasm_js: each run's fresh seed from the host's crypto.getRandomValues, since no seed is pinned (QR-14d)

whiteboard-native-fixture.description: a minimal native binary built with the dist-native profile, so the release gates (harden-check, repro-check, cargo-auditable, third-party notices) run against a real artifact until whiteboard-daemon replaces it

whiteboard-port-fakes.description: in-memory fakes of the ports for tests: a fixed clock, a sequential id mint, a FIFO keyed lock and a std-only block_on; a dev-dependency only

whiteboard-fuzz.description: cargo-fuzz targets, one per untrusted-input entry (OKF/JSON Canvas/OCIF/markdown parsers, sync frames, HTTP and MCP JSON-RPC, loro import, wasm-boundary JSON, font files). Nightly toolchain only (libFuzzer, sanitizers), so it is a workspace of its own, excluded from the root one; its library half builds on stable to replay committed regressions

allowedThirdParty.libfuzzer-sys: the libFuzzer driver cargo-fuzz links each target against; optional, so the target bodies build on stable
